# ak command reference

<!-- Generated by `make docs` from the command table. Do not edit. -->

Usage: `ak <command> [options] [arguments]`. Options may come before or after arguments, and short options can be combined (`-ea` is `-e -a`). Commands that talk to a device pick it with `-s/--serial`, then `$ANDROID_SERIAL`; with one device connected it is used, with several you are asked (or `-a/--all` where supported). Results go to stdout and messages to stderr. Exit codes: 0 success, 1 failure, 2 usage error, 130 interrupted.

- **APK:** [install](#ak-install), [extract](#ak-extract), [signature](#ak-signature)
- **App:** [info](#ak-info), [permissions](#ak-permissions), [launch](#ak-launch), [kill](#ak-kill), [clear](#ak-clear), [uninstall](#ak-uninstall), [restart](#ak-restart), [activities](#ak-activities), [logcat](#ak-logcat)

## ak install

Install APK files.

```
ak install [options] [apk|directory...]
```

Install APK files on one or more devices.
APK files given by name are installed; with a directory or no argument, pick APKs (newest first).
Common failures are handled automatically: test-only APKs are retried with -t, downgrades
with -d, and when that is not allowed or the signature differs, ak offers to uninstall first.
If '&lt;file&gt;.apk.idsig' exists, --no-incremental is added.

**Arguments**

| Argument | Description |
|---|---|
| `apk` | APK files to install |
| `directory` | Pick APKs from these directories |

**Options**

| Option | Description |
|---|---|
| `-l, --latest` | Install the newest APK (in the current or given directory) |
| `-e, --every-apk` | Install every APK (in the current or given directory) |
| `-f, --filter WORDS` | Pick among APKs whose names contain all the words |
| `-r` | Replace the existing app, keeping its data (always on) |
| `-t, --test-only` | Allow test-only APKs |
| `-d, --downgrade` | Allow version downgrade |
| `-y, --yes` | Uninstall and reinstall without asking when a device refuses the update (removes the app's data) |
| `-s, --serial ID` | Target device; repeat for more (default: $ANDROID_SERIAL, or ask) |
| `-a, --all` | All connected devices |
| `-h, --help` | Show this help |

**Examples**

```bash
ak install
ak install app-debug.apk
ak install -l build/outputs/apk/debug
ak install -f "myapp release"
ak install app.apk --all
ak install -e build/outputs/apk --all
ak install app.apk -s emulator-5554 -y
```

## ak extract

Extract APK file from device.

```
ak extract [options] [package] [file]
```

Save the APK of an installed package to a local file.
The arguments can be given in either order: a value ending in .apk or containing '/' is the file.

**Arguments**

| Argument | Description |
|---|---|
| `package` | Package name (default: the foreground app) |
| `file` | Output file (default: &lt;package&gt;.apk) |

**Options**

| Option | Description |
|---|---|
| `-s, --serial ID` | Target device (default: $ANDROID_SERIAL, or ask) |
| `-h, --help` | Show this help |

**Examples**

```bash
ak extract
ak extract myapp.apk
ak extract com.example.app
ak extract com.example.app out.apk
```

## ak signature

Extract signature hash.

```
ak signature [options] [package|file.apk]
```

Show the signing certificate (DN, SHA-256, SHA-1, MD5) of an installed package or a local APK.
No Android SDK is needed; apksigner is used only if the APK cannot be parsed.
Without an argument, pick from the foreground apps of connected devices and APKs in the current directory.

**Arguments**

| Argument | Description |
|---|---|
| `package` | Package installed on the device |
| `file.apk` | Local APK file |

**Options**

| Option | Description |
|---|---|
| `-s, --serial ID` | Target device (default: $ANDROID_SERIAL, or ask) |
| `--json` | Print the result as JSON |
| `-h, --help` | Show this help |

**Examples**

```bash
ak signature
ak signature com.example.app
ak signature app-release.apk
ak signature app.apk --json | jq -r '.signers[0].sha256'
```

## ak restart

Restart an app and time its launch.

```
ak restart [options] [package]
```

Force-stop an app, start its launcher activity again and show how long the launch took
(am start -W: TotalTime). With --repeat, restart several times and show min/avg/max.

**Arguments**

| Argument | Description |
|---|---|
| `package` | Package name (default: the foreground app) |

**Options**

| Option | Description |
|---|---|
| `-r, --repeat N` | Restart N times (default 1) |
| `-s, --serial ID` | Target device (default: $ANDROID_SERIAL, or ask) |
| `--json` | Print the result as JSON |
| `-h, --help` | Show this help |

**Examples**

```bash
ak restart
ak restart com.example.app -r 5
ak restart --json
```

## ak logcat

Show logs of one app.

```
ak logcat [options] [package]
```

Show the logcat lines of one app and keep following it when it restarts (new process IDs
are picked up automatically; processes like 'pkg:remote' are included). The app's lines still
in the device log buffer are shown first (use -c to start empty). Press Ctrl+C to stop.

**Arguments**

| Argument | Description |
|---|---|
| `package` | Package name (default: the foreground app) |

**Options**

| Option | Description |
|---|---|
| `-l, --level LEVEL` | Minimum level: V, D, I, W, E or F (default V) |
| `-c, --clear` | Clear the device log buffer first |
| `-s, --serial ID` | Target device (default: $ANDROID_SERIAL, or ask) |
| `-h, --help` | Show this help |

**Examples**

```bash
ak logcat
ak logcat com.example.app -l W
ak logcat -c > app.log
```

## ak screenshot

Save a screenshot.

```
ak screenshot [options] [file|directory]
```

Capture the screen and save it as PNG on this computer (nothing is left on the device).
The default name is screenshot-&lt;model&gt;-&lt;time&gt;.png in the current directory.
With several devices, one file per device is saved. Saved paths are printed to stdout.
-c copies the image to the clipboard instead of saving it; give a file or directory
(or -o) to save it as well.

**Arguments**

| Argument | Description |
|---|---|
| `file` | Output .png file (one device) |
| `directory` | Save into this directory |

**Options**

| Option | Description |
|---|---|
| `-c, --copy` | Copy the image to the clipboard (alone: no file is saved) |
| `-o, --open` | Open the saved file with the default app |
| `-s, --serial ID` | Target device; repeat for more (default: $ANDROID_SERIAL, or ask) |
| `-a, --all` | All connected devices |
| `-h, --help` | Show this help |

**Examples**

```bash
ak screenshot
ak screenshot -o
ak screenshot -c
ak screenshot -c ~/Desktop
ak screenshot home.png
ak screenshot ~/Desktop --all
```

## ak record

Record the screen.

```
ak record [options] [file|directory]
```

Record the screen to MP4 until you press Ctrl+C or the time limit is reached, then save the
video on this computer and delete it from the device. Android limits one recording to
180 seconds and does not record audio. The saved path is printed to stdout.

**Arguments**

| Argument | Description |
|---|---|
| `file` | Output .mp4 file (default: record-&lt;model&gt;-&lt;time&gt;.mp4) |
| `directory` | Save into this directory |

**Options**

| Option | Description |
|---|---|
| `-t, --time-limit SECONDS` | Stop after this many seconds (1-180, default 180) |
| `--size WxH` | Video size, e.g. 1280x720 (default: screen size) |
| `-o, --open` | Open the saved file with the default app |
| `-s, --serial ID` | Target device (default: $ANDROID_SERIAL, or ask) |
| `-h, --help` | Show this help |

**Examples**

```bash
ak record
ak record -o
ak record bug.mp4
ak record -t 30 --size 720x1600
```

## ak pull

Pull recent files from device.

```
ak pull [options] [directory]
```

Pick recently modified files on the device (like the Files app 'Recents' tab, via MediaStore)
and pull them. Files keep their names; existing local files are overwritten, and selected
files with the same name get a ' (N)' suffix. Shows the 300 newest files.

**Arguments**

| Argument | Description |
|---|---|
| `directory` | Where to save (default: current directory; created after confirmation) |

**Options**

| Option | Description |
|---|---|
| `-y, --yes` | Create the destination directory without asking if it does not exist |
| `-s, --serial ID` | Target device (default: $ANDROID_SERIAL, or ask) |
| `-h, --help` | Show this help |

**Examples**

```bash
ak pull
ak pull ~/Downloads/device
ak pull new-dir -y
```

## ak devices

Show connected devices.

```
ak devices [options]
```

List connected devices with model, Android version, CPU ABI and state.
ABI shows 32/64-bit app support: (64/32), (64only) or (32only).

**Options**

| Option | Description |
|---|---|
| `--json` | Print the result as JSON |
| `-h, --help` | Show this help |

**Examples**

```bash
ak devices
ak devices --json
```

## ak mac

Show device MAC addresses.

```
ak mac [options]
```

Show the MAC addresses of a device.
  Wi-Fi (current)  MAC of the current connection (per network, may be randomized)
  Wi-Fi (factory)  The device's own Wi-Fi MAC, if exposed (also when Wi-Fi is off)
  Bluetooth        Bluetooth MAC

**Options**

| Option | Description |
|---|---|
| `-s, --serial ID` | Target device; repeat for more (default: $ANDROID_SERIAL, or ask) |
| `-a, --all` | All connected devices |
| `--json` | Print the result as JSON |
| `-h, --help` | Show this help |

**Examples**

```bash
ak mac
ak mac --all
ak mac --json
```

## ak wifi

Debug over Wi-Fi.

```
ak wifi [options] [off]
```

Switch a USB-connected device to Wi-Fi debugging (adb tcpip) and connect to it, so the
cable can be unplugged. The computer and the device must be on the same network.
'ak wifi off' switches Wi-Fi devices back to USB mode and disconnects them.
The connected address is printed to stdout.

**Arguments**

| Argument | Description |
|---|---|
| `off` | Switch back to USB and disconnect |

**Options**

| Option | Description |
|---|---|
| `-p, --port PORT` | TCP port (default 5555) |
| `-s, --serial ID` | Target device (default: $ANDROID_SERIAL, or ask) |
| `-h, --help` | Show this help |

**Examples**

```bash
ak wifi
ak wifi -s emulator-5554
ak wifi off
```

## ak doctor

Diagnose adb setup.

```
ak doctor [options]
```

Check the adb ak uses, other adb binaries, connected devices, shell completion and optional tools.
Lookup order: AK_ADB, ANDROID_HOME, ANDROID_SDK_ROOT, PATH, Android Studio default SDK, ~/.ak/platform-tools.
Running adb binaries of different versions side by side restarts the adb server and drops device connections.
[✓] fine, [!] worth fixing, [✗] a problem. Exits 1 when a problem is found.

**Options**

| Option | Description |
|---|---|
| `-v, --verbose` | Show all details |
| `--json` | Print the result as JSON |
| `-h, --help` | Show this help |

**Examples**

```bash
ak doctor
ak doctor -v
ak doctor --json
```

## ak completion

Print a shell completion script.

```
ak completion [options] <shell>
```

Print the tab completion script for zsh, bash, fish or PowerShell.
Homebrew installs bash, zsh and fish completion; 'ak doctor' shows how to set up the others.

**Arguments**

| Argument | Description |
|---|---|
| `shell` | zsh, bash, fish or powershell |

**Options**

| Option | Description |
|---|---|
| `-h, --help` | Show this help |

**Examples**

```bash
source <(ak completion zsh)          # in ~/.zshrc, after compinit
eval "$(ak completion bash)"         # in ~/.bashrc
ak completion fish > ~/.config/fish/completions/ak.fish
ak completion powershell | Out-String | Invoke-Expression   # in $PROFILE
```

## Global options

| Option | Description |
|---|---|
| `-h, --help` | Show help |
| `-v, --version` | Show version |
| `--no-color` | Disable colored output |

| Environment | Description |
|---|---|
| `ANDROID_SERIAL` | Default target device |
| `AK_ADB` | Path to the adb binary |
| `NO_COLOR` | Disable colored output |
| `AK_DEBUG` | Set to 1 to write a debug log to $TMPDIR/ak-debug.log (AK_DEBUG_LOG changes the path) |
